hints: Apply conservation of linear momentum to the collision between A ($4\text{ kg}$) and B ($2\text{ kg}$).
Let the speed of B after the collision be $v_B$. The speed of A is then $v_A = 0.5v_B$.
Form the equation $4(10) + 2(0) = 4(0.5v_B) + 2v_B$ and solve for $v_B$.
walkthrough:
State the principle of conservation of linear momentum for an isolated system:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
Here sphere A has mass $m_A = 4\text{ kg}$ and initial velocity $u_A = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, while sphere B has mass $m_B = 2\text{ kg}$ and starts at rest ($u_B = 0$).

Express the speed of A after impact in terms of the speed of B: $v_A = \frac{1}{2}v_B = 0.5v_B$. Substitute all quantities into the momentum equation:
$$4(10) + 2(0) = 4(0.5v_B) + 2v_B$$

Divide both sides by $4$:
$$v_B = \frac{40}{4} = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
(Note that $v_A = 0.5(10) = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

hints: Sphere B (mass $2\text{ kg}$, speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$) collides directly with stationary sphere C (mass $1\text{ kg}$).
After this collision, the speed of B is one third the speed of C: $v_C = 3v_B$.
Apply conservation of momentum: $2(10) + 1(0) = 2v_B + 1(3v_B)$ to find $v_B = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Compare the speed of A ($v_A = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$) moving behind B with $v_B = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to deduce that A will catch B.
walkthrough: First, analyze the second collision between sphere B and the third sphere C. Sphere B has mass $m_B = 2\text{ kg}$ and enters with speed $u_B = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Sphere C has mass $m_C = 1\text{ kg}$ and is initially at rest ($u_C = 0$).
State the given relationship between post-collision velocities: $v_B = \frac{1}{3}v_C$, which means $v_C = 3v_B$.

Apply conservation of linear momentum for the system containing B and C:
$$m_B u_B + m_C u_C = m_B v_B + m_C v_C$$
$$2(10) + 1(0) = 2v_B + 1(3v_B)$$
$$20 = 5v_B$$
Divide by $5$:
$$v_B = \frac{20}{5} = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
(and $v_C = 3(4) = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$).
Recall the speed of sphere A from part (a): $v_A = 0.5(10) = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Sphere A is travelling behind sphere B along the same straight line.

Compare the two speeds:
$$v_A = 5\text{ m s}^{-1} > v_B = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Because sphere A is moving faster than sphere B ahead of it, the distance between them decreases to zero, guaranteeing a subsequent collision between A and B.

hints: Apply conservation of momentum to the collision where A ($4\text{ kg}$ at $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and B ($2\text{ kg}$ at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$) coalesce.
Find the common velocity $v = \frac{14}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ of the combined mass ($6\text{ kg}$).
Calculate the initial kinetic energy of the entire system before any collisions: $\frac{1}{2}m_A u_A^2 = \frac{1}{2}(4)(10^2) = 200\text{ J}$.
Calculate the final kinetic energy of the system (coalesced AB plus sphere C moving at $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$), and subtract it from $200\text{ J}$.
walkthrough: First, determine the velocity of the coalesced particle formed by A and B in their second collision. Before this collision, $v_A = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_B = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

State conservation of linear momentum for A and B:
$$m_A v_A + m_B v_B = (m_A + m_B)v$$
Substitute $m_A = 4\text{ kg}$ and $m_B = 2\text{ kg}$:
$$4(5) + 2(4) = (4 + 2)v$$
$$20 + 8 = 6v$$
$$28 = 6v$$
Divide by $6$ and simplify:
$$v = \frac{28}{6} = \frac{14}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the total initial kinetic energy of the entire system before any collision occurred. Only sphere A was moving ($u_A = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$), while B and C were at rest:
$$E_{k, \text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}m_A u_A^2 = \frac{1}{2}(4)(10^2) = 2 \times 100 = 200\text{ J}$$

Calculate the total final kinetic energy of the system after all three collisions. The system now consists of the combined body AB ($m = 6\text{ kg}$) moving at $\frac{14}{3}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and sphere C ($m = 1\text{ kg}$) moving at $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}m_{AB} v_{AB}^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_C v_C^2$$
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(6)\left(\frac{14}{3}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{2}(1)(12^2)$$
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = 3\left(\frac{196}{9}\right) + \frac{1}{2}(144) = \frac{196}{3} + 72$$
Express with a common denominator of $3$:
$$72 = \frac{216}{3}$$
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{196 + 216}{3} = \frac{412}{3}\text{ J}$$

Calculate the total loss of kinetic energy by subtracting final kinetic energy from initial kinetic energy:
$$\text{Loss} = E_{k, \text{initial}} - E_{k, \text{final}} = 200 - \frac{412}{3}$$
$$200 = \frac{600}{3}$$
$$\text{Loss} = \frac{600 - 412}{3} = \frac{188}{3}\text{ J} \approx 62.7\text{ J}$$
